cases.name: null-forms
cases.notes: §4: every null spelling and the empty value → type null, all value columns null.
cases.source:
---
a: null
b: Null
c: NULL
d: ~
e:
---

# T

cases.name: empty-quoted-is-empty-string
cases.notes: §4: quoted empties are strings, not null.

cases.name: core-booleans
cases.notes: §4: the six core-schema spellings → bool.
cases.source:
---
a: true
b: True
c: TRUE
d: false
e: False
f: FALSE
---

# T

cases.name: yaml-1-1-booleans-are-strings
cases.notes: §4: 1.1 booleans are not core schema → type string.
cases.source:
---
a: yes
b: no
c: on
d: off
e: y
f: n
g: Yes
h: OFF
---

# T

cases.name: int-forms
cases.notes: §4: decimal with leading zeros is decimal (012 = 12), `0o` octal, `0x` hex, signs.

cases.name: non-core-int-spellings-are-strings
cases.notes: §4: underscores (1.1), binary, a signed hex, an out-of-range octal digit → strings.

cases.name: float-forms
cases.notes: §4: the core float regex; `1.0` is the number 1; `1e21` stores as 1e21.

cases.name: non-finite-floats
cases.notes: §4 / §8: ±Infinity store as REAL infinities (fixture strings "Infinity"/"-Infinity"); NaN binds as NULL, so a number row with null val_num is NaN (fixture "NaN"). The read shapes see ±Infinity and, for NaN, null.
cases.source:
---
a: .inf
b: -.inf
c: .nan
d: +.inf
e: .Inf
f: .NaN
g: .INF
h: -.Inf
---

# T

cases.name: infinity-and-nan-words-are-strings
cases.notes: §4: only the dotted spellings are non-finite floats; these words are plain strings.
cases.source:
---
a: Infinity
b: NaN
c: inf
d: nan
e: -Infinity
---

# T

cases.name: large-int-precision
cases.notes: §4: integers are IEEE doubles — 2^53+1 reads as 2^53; 2^64-1 rounds to 18446744073709552000.

cases.name: timestamps-are-strings
cases.notes: §4: no timestamp type in the core schema — every ISO form is type string (and none of these is range-shaped).

cases.name: quoted-scalars-are-strings
cases.notes: §4 / §2.2: quoting makes a string — but range detection is on the string, so the quoted `"1..5"` still gets a range side channel.

cases.name: str-tag
cases.notes: §4: `!!str` pins a string.
cases.source:
---
a: !!str 1
b: !!str true
c: !!str 2026-01-01
d: !!str null
e: !!str 1.5
---

# T

cases.name: explicit-core-tags-that-resolve
cases.notes: §4: a core tag whose value matches that tag's own format resolves as tagged.
cases.source:
---
a: !!int "1"
b: !!float "1.5"
c: !!bool "true"
d: !!null ""
e: !!float 1.0
f: !!int 12
g: !!null null
---

# T

cases.name: explicit-core-tag-mismatch-is-a-string
cases.notes: §4 (as built): when the value does not match the tag's format the `yaml` package warns (unresolved tag) and yields the plain STRING — `!!float 1` is "1", `!!int 1.5` is "1.5", `!!null x` is "x". The README's 'resolve as tagged' holds only for matching values.
cases.source:
---
a: !!int 1.5
b: !!bool yes
c: !!float 1
d: !!null x
e: !!int "abc"
---

# T

cases.name: unknown-tag-yields-the-string
cases.notes: §4 (as built): an unknown tag is a warning and the node resolves as a STRING of its source — `!custom 1` is "1", not the number 1; `!bar` with no value is "".
cases.source:
---
a: !custom 1
b: !custom text
c: !foo true
d: !bar
---

# T

cases.name: anchors-and-aliases
cases.notes: §4: aliases resolve to the anchored value (scalars, sequences, mappings).

cases.name: merge-key-is-ordinary
cases.notes: §4: `<<` is not merged in 1.2 — it flattens as the key `m.<<.k`.

cases.name: block-scalars
cases.notes: §4: literal keeps line breaks and the final one; folded joins lines; `-` strips, `+` keeps trailing blank lines.
cases.source:
---
a: |
  line1
  line2
b: >
  folded
  text
c: |-
  strip
d: |+
  keep

e: >-
  f
  g
---

# T

cases.name: plain-multiline-and-quoted-escapes
cases.notes: §4: plain scalars fold across lines; single quotes double; double quotes escape.
cases.source:
---
a: first
  second
b: 'it''s'
c: "esc\n"
d: "\u00e9"
e: "tab\t"
---

# T

cases.name: flow-collections
cases.notes: §2.3 over flow syntax: same flattening as block syntax; `c: {}` vanishes.

cases.name: quoted-and-spaced-keys
cases.notes: §2.3: keys are not trimmed or case-folded; a quoted `a.b` is indistinguishable from a nested one.

cases.name: comments-ignored
cases.notes: §4: comments are not content.
cases.source:
---
# leading comment
a: 1 # trailing
# between
b: two
---

# T

cases.name: duplicate-keys-no-rows
cases.notes: §4 failures: duplicate keys in one mapping → parse error → no frontmatter rows; the body still computes.

cases.name: tab-indentation-no-rows
cases.notes: §4 failures: tabs as indentation → no frontmatter rows.

cases.name: document-end-marker-no-rows
cases.notes: §4 failures: `...` ends the first document and `b: 2` starts another → 'multiple documents' → no rows. (A `---` line cannot occur inside the fence: it closes it — see frontmatter::yaml-line-starting-with-dashes-is-inside-the-fence for the `---x` non-marker.)

cases.name: directive-then-marker-no-rows
cases.notes: §4 failures: a directive line and a `--- x` marker inside the fence — the `yaml` package rejects the document, so no rows.

cases.name: sequence-document-no-rows
cases.notes: §3.1: the result is not a mapping → no frontmatter rows.

cases.name: scalar-document-no-rows
cases.notes: §3.1: a scalar document → no frontmatter rows.

cases.name: syntax-error-no-rows
cases.notes: §4 failures: unclosed flow collections → no rows.
